units.summary: The estimated freight document volume is about 1,200 documents per day across all sites; the notes say this should be checked against volume data.
units.quote: Mikko estimated about 1,200 documents per day across all sites.

units.summary: The TMS document log was estimated to show around 1,000 documents per normal working day, with the count depending on how scanned paper documents are counted.
units.quote: I would say it's a bit less, maybe around 1,000 on a normal working day according to the TMS document log.

units.topic: freight document input channels and languages
units.summary: Freight documents arrive as email attachments, driver-app photos and paper at warehouse gates. They are in Finnish, Swedish, English, Estonian, and some Polish and Lithuanian.
units.quote: Documents arrive as email attachments (PDF, some JPG photos taken by drivers), via the driver app (photos) and on paper at the warehouse gates.

units.summary: The fields entered from freight documents include shipment and customer references, sender and receiver, package count, gross weight, pallet information, delivery date and time, signature presence, and remarks.
units.quote: Fields entered: shipment/consignment number, customer reference, sender, receiver, number of packages, gross weight, pallet count and type, delivery date and time, signature present Y/N, remarks (damage, shortages).

units.summary: The estimated manual-entry error rate is around 4%, and handwritten damage or shortage remarks on PODs can be missed.
units.quote: Mikko's estimate of the error rate in manual entry: around 4 %. Errors lead to wrong invoices, credit notes, and disputes; the finance team spends "a day a week" on corrections.

units.topic: freight document processing history and log access
units.summary: The TMS document log contains about 1.5 million registered freight-document entries and can be exported as a report CSV, up to 100,000 rows. Paper-document registration date is the scan date.
units.quote: RouteLine TMS | Document log (registered freight documents) | 2019-06 | approx. 1.5 M entries | Cloud database | Report export (CSV), max 100,000 rows | Operations Director | Registration date = scan date for paper documents

units.summary: The archive contains about 1.5 million scanned freight-document PDFs, but they are image-only, have no index, and use inconsistent filenames.
units.quote: Document archive | Scanned freight documents | 2019-06 | approx. 1.5 M PDF files, 2.3 TB | PDF (image only, no text layer) | File share | No owner | No index; file names inconsistent; mixed quality

units.topic: POD image data availability and quality
units.summary: The driver app has about 400,000 POD photos and signatures stored as JPGs in the TMS; quality issues include night photos, blur and partial documents.
units.quote: Driver app | POD photos and signatures | 2020-05 | approx. 400 k images | JPG in TMS | Via TMS | Operations Director | Night photos, blur, partial documents

units.topic: TMS data access for freight processing
units.summary: The TMS holds transport orders, shipments, POD status and freight costs, with a single-record REST API; bulk export is a paid service.
units.quote: RouteLine TMS | Transport orders, shipments, POD status, freight costs | 2018-03 | approx. 1.4 M shipments | Cloud database | REST API, single records; bulk export as paid service | Operations Director | Customer IDs differ from Business Central

units.summary: The proposed forecast would cover daily inbound pallets and outbound order lines per warehouse, using WMS history, customer forecasts, calendar effects and possibly weather for chilled-food customers.
units.quote: Idea: forecast daily inbound pallets and outbound order lines per warehouse 1-3 weeks ahead, using history from the WMS plus customer forecasts, calendar effects (holidays, campaigns), and maybe weather for the chilled food customers.

units.summary: The WMS has about 48 million transaction rows covering receipts, putaways, picks, shipments and inventory movements, accessible through read-only SQL. Pre-2020 data has an old structure, and pallet types are inconsistent.
units.quote: WMS | Receipts, putaways, picks, shipments, inventory movements | 2020-01 | approx. 48 M transaction rows | SQL Server tables | Read-only SQL (IT Manager) | Operations Director | Pre-2020 data in old structure; pallet types inconsistent

units.summary: Customer forecasts comprise irregular weekly volume forecasts from about 12 customers, supplied as Excel attachments in email; formats differ and forecasts are often missing.
units.quote: Customer forecasts | Weekly volume forecasts from customers | 2022 | approx. 12 customers, irregular | Excel attachments in email | Manual | Site managers | Different formats per customer; often missing

units.summary: Only about a third of key customers send forecasts regularly.
units.quote: Only about a third of the key customers send forecasts regularly.

units.summary: The proposed customer-service workflow would classify incoming emails, route them, look up shipment status in the TMS and draft replies for an agent to approve; automatic replies were not wanted at this stage.
units.quote: Idea: automatically classify incoming emails, route them, look up shipment status from the TMS and draft a reply for the agent to approve.

units.summary: The shared Outlook mailbox contains about 300,000 emails, accessible through Microsoft Graph; no categories are stored.
units.quote: Outlook shared mailbox | Customer service emails | 2021-01 | approx. 300 k emails | Exchange Online | Microsoft Graph | Customer Service Team Lead | Personal data of consumers; no categories stored

units.summary: A customer-service category tally is available for one tally week per month from April through September 2026.
units.quote: CS_Email_Tally - customer service mailbox category tally (one tally week per month), Apr - Sep 2026.

units.summary: Customer-service emails can contain consumers’ names, phone numbers and home-delivery addresses, creating data-processing and transparency considerations for the proposed use case.
units.quote: Emails contain personal data (names, phone numbers, home delivery addresses of consumers for e-commerce customers).

units.summary: The current TMS route-planning module does not account for customers’ actual unloading times, so planners often override it.
units.quote: The TMS has a built-in route planning module. Planners use it for Vantaa-area distribution but override it often because "it does not know the customers' unloading times".

units.summary: Telematics provides about 120 million vehicle position points, including fuel and driving-event data, via CSV export; the data is not linked to shipments.
units.quote: Telematics | Vehicle position, fuel, driving events | 2019-09 | approx. 120 M position points | Vendor cloud | CSV export | Fleet manager | Not linked to shipments

conflicts.description: The meeting notes give an estimate of about 1,200 documents per day across all sites. The recording gives a lower estimate of around 1,000 on a normal working day according to the TMS document log. The sources do not establish which estimate to follow, so the discrepancy is unresolved.
